players.product: Gemma Power Systems EPC for combined-cycle gas plants serving data-center load (4.1 GW in backlog) plus data-center thermal expansion / energy storage tank fabrication

quarterly_data.signal: Segment detail for Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended April 30, 2026), given on the call: power segment revenues $227 million, 78% of total, pre-tax book income $52 million and backlog of $2.5 billion; industrial segment revenue $58 million (20% of consolidated revenues, a record for the segment) with backlog of $225 million; teledata revenue $6 million with backlog of $8 million. Segment gross margins were 23.6% (power), 11.8% (industrial) and 11% (teledata).
quarterly_data.figure: power $227 million (78%), backlog $2.5 billion; industrial $58 million, backlog $225 million; gross margins 23.6% / 11.8% / 11%

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog mix: CEO said the backlog is approximately 79% natural gas projects, 13% renewable and 8% industrial, and that with current demand for natural gas-fired facilities, complex combined cycle projects are expected to represent the majority of backlog for the near and midterm; renewable demand 'has softened' but Argan will keep renewable capabilities. Current backlog includes four gas-fired power plants in the United States totaling over 4.1 GW.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog approximately 79% natural gas, 13% renewable, 8% industrial; four gas-fired plants totaling over 4.1 GW

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline and capacity (point-in-time guidance): management expects to add 'a handful of new projects over the next 10-18 months' and reiterated that capacity is 10 to 12 jobs simultaneously; there are currently eight power jobs underway (six thermal and two renewables). Asked whether $2 billion of revenue is achievable, the CEO said 'The answer is yes, down the road', but gave no guidance on capacity growth timing, noting that hiring and training take time. Developers still must clear air permits, access to gas, water permits, turbines and financing; no change seen in developer behavior.
quarterly_data.figure: handful of new projects over the next 10-18 months; capacity 10 to 12 jobs; eight power jobs underway (six thermal, two renewables)

quarterly_data.signal: Project status: substantial completion ahead of schedule on the third and final Midwest Solar and Battery project, and final completion of the 950 MW Trumbull Energy Center in Ohio. In Texas, the 1.2 GW ultra-efficient combined cycle plant for SLEC is progressing well, construction is beginning to ramp at the 1.4 GW project with CPV and the 860 MW project, and the 700 MW combined cycle plant in the U.S. is moving forward as expected. In Ireland, the 300 MW Tarbert Next Generation biofuel plant for SSE Thermal and a 170 MW thermal facility are progressing.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.2 GW SLEC; 1.4 GW CPV; 860 MW; 700 MW; 950 MW Trumbull final completion; 300 MW Tarbert + 170 MW in Ireland

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center fabrication expansion: the industrial segment has a $125 million data center project (contract awarded in November of 2025 for fabrication of thermal expansion and energy storage tanks) and management sees 'a multi-year runway' for data-center thermal expansion tank opportunities. Argan broke ground in late April on an additional fabrication facility in North Carolina, about 20 miles from the existing (full-bore) facility, targeted to produce tanks later this year; the CEO estimated the investment in the '$10 million-$13 million range' and expects industrial revenue to meaningfully exceed the previous year.
quarterly_data.figure: $125 million data center project; new NC fabrication facility capex $10 million-$13 million

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog additions outside major awards: while $550 million in revenues was converted over the last couple of quarters, Argan added $215 million in Q4 and over $125 million in Q1 from new and add-on jobs in the industrial and teledata segments plus change orders. Net liquidity of $421 million (cash and investments $974 million, no debt) is said to support the $2.8 billion backlog and 'several billion more in backlog over time'.
quarterly_data.figure: $215 million added in Q4; over $125 million added in Q1; net liquidity $421 million

quarterly_data.signal: Margin outlook and pricing: CEO said consolidated blended margins 'tend to be in the high teens and low 20s' and it is too early to tell ultimate margins on major jobs in early phases; early completions (Trumbull, Midwest Solar) helped the 21% blended rate. Job pricing is rising with inflation and market conditions, making each build a bigger job; only a handful of firms can do gigawatt-plus combined cycle jobs, and pricing for IPP versus utility customers is not expected to be meaningfully different.
quarterly_data.figure: blended margins high teens and low 20s; Q1 blended rate 21%

quarterly_data.signal: Capital return: the board increased the buyback authorization to $200 million from $150 million and extended it through January 31st, 2030; $33.6 million was returned to shareholders in Q1 and approximately $116.7 million has been returned through repurchases since inception; quarterly dividend $0.50 per share.
quarterly_data.figure: buyback authorization $200 million (from $150 million); $33.6 million returned in Q1
